definitions.explanation: Single-use chopsticks made of wood or bamboo that come joined together and need to be split apart before use.

examples.japanese: {割|わ}り{箸|ばし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけて→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。

examples.english: I'm bad at splitting disposable chopsticks.

examples.japanese: ⟦{環境|かんきょう}→環境：00174_kankyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{割|わ}り{箸|ばし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}わない→使う：00473_tsukau⟧ようにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: I try not to use disposable chopsticks for environmental reasons.

notes:
{割|わ}り{箸|ばし} literally means "chopsticks you split apart" (⟦{割|わ}る→割る：02334_waru⟧ = to split). They are the standard single-use chopsticks provided at convenience stores, takeout restaurants, and food stalls in Japan.

ETYMOLOGY:
From ⟦{割|わ}る→割る：02334_waru⟧ (to split) + ⟦{箸|はし}→箸：01026_hashi⟧ (chopsticks). The two sticks come connected and must be pulled apart before use.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {割|わ}り{箸|ばし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{割|わ}る→割る：02334_waru⟧ (to split disposable chopsticks)
- {割|わ}り{箸|ばし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧ (to use disposable chopsticks)
- {割|わ}り{箸|ばし}{入|い}れ (chopstick holder/dispenser)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Environmental concerns have led to a マイ⟦{箸|はし}→箸：01026_hashi⟧ ("my chopsticks") movement, where people carry their own reusable chopsticks. Some convenience stores now ask if you need {割|わ}り{箸|ばし} rather than including them automatically.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦お{箸|はし}→お箸：10275_ohashi⟧: chopsticks (polite)
- マイ⟦{箸|はし}→箸：01026_hashi⟧: personal reusable chopsticks
- ⟦{箸置|はしお}き→箸置き：04481_hashioki⟧: chopstick rest
